column3: So here's what I'd suggest. This part isn't from the studies. It's just what they made me think about.
One. Notice the words, I'll check later. That's often the ostrich talking.
Two. Before you look at a result, decide what would change your mind. Then you can't move the goalposts afterwards.
Three. If a result gives you an answer you hate, ask yourself: would I be retesting if it said what I wanted?
And four. Be kind to yourself when you catch it. Everybody does this. Catching it is the whole skill.
Remember the, I'm fine, from the start? Next time you say it, take one honest second, and check.
Tell me in the comments: what's one thing you've been not clicking on?
This is Social Ripple. See you next time.
